doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: Nerve-wracking film dates
summary: Film dates on a soundstage with click tracks, a conductor and many players made him tense.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Well let’s talk more about, do you recall the most challenging studio date you ever did, or something along that line?

Any time I got called to do a film date. I may have — I tried to keep as cool a demeanor as I could. And I didn’t get too many but there was a few along the way. Until you actually see, you walk in and see what’s on the stand in front of you, you’re kind of thinking okay, I hope this is not like a thousand notes and that there are no changes and that I have to play this thing exactly as written, which turned out I kind of didn’t. And the

composers were pretty cool even if the charts were pretty specific they wanted you to make music out of it so they weren’t too rigid about that. But you know when you’re sitting there with 40 or 50 other musicians on a soundstage at SONY, you don’t want to be the one screwing up the take for any reason. Because heads will turn. So those dates were nerve wracking for me. And I can’t honestly say I enjoyed it all that much. It was very kind of pressure-packed. And fortunately I didn’t hold anyone up, so that worked out okay. But they were tense for me.
Were you hearing a click track?
Yeah. A lot of times, most everything we did was cut to click. So you’re trying to interpret this music and play with the drummer and play with the click —
And watch the conductor, and it’s challenging.
